components.label: Collection, refresh, search and pagination
components.behavior: Tasks defaults to All unless a valid view query is supplied. Visible search, Status and Sort are independent; sorting is stable by importance or account-local scheduled time (undated last). Reads use a latest-request guard. Active and Completed lists page independently at 8 rows, or 4 below 600px. Tags appear under More filters when available. Creating retains the current view/search/status/page and offers an Open task result link.

components.label: Task row: completion, Today, week, importance stars and the ⋯ menu
components.behavior: Aligned checkbox/content/actions keep the task name primary and parent chips sized to content; the name and Edit open the floating editor in place (a modified click opens the Task page). Facts distinguish status, localized due date/Due today, manual Today selection and scheduled interval/start/occurrence in the account timezone. Week (pin) and Today (sun) stay inline as icon toggles with hover labels and accessible names, followed by 1–5 importance stars (a keyboard radio group: click a star or use the arrow keys); the ⋯ menu lists Due date, Remind me, Repeat, Edit and Archive with labels and closes on outside click, Escape or a choice. Archive retains data. Automatic Today membership cannot be removed through a manual-selection action. Overdue rows show a red edge and facts line.

components.label: Group by Goal
components.behavior: Tasks stays the execution view: the time filters (Today, This week…) and Status apply first, then Group by Goal splits the result into one collapsible section per Goal (a Milestone Task belongs to its Milestone's Goal), each with its count and Open roadmap, and a trailing Inbox. Inside a Goal, Tasks follow the roadmap (Milestone position, then Tasks directly in the Goal) under one subheading per Milestone; Sort orders Tasks within a Milestone. Grouped lists are not paged. Group by Goal is the default; choosing No grouping is remembered per browser.

components.label: Today
components.behavior: Includes explicit account-local daily selections, matching deadline/start/occurrence dates, overlapping work intervals and unfinished overdue work not yet in History. Explicit daily selection can reveal historical work deliberately. Add for today from a Task row also selects the current week and changes no Task dates/status. Task-row add/remove actions use +/check icons with native hover labels and accessible names.

components.label: Next
components.behavior: Includes any future deadline/start/occurrence/scheduled date, including scheduled end. A Task can appear in both Today and Next.

components.label: This week
components.behavior: Membership is the explicit current Monday-week selection set, including historical or completed selected work. Completion does not remove a selection. Selecting a Task for Today adds weekly membership atomically; automatic date-based Today membership alone does not select the week.

components.label: Overdue
components.behavior: Shows fetched active unfinished Tasks with a deadline before the account-local today, including historical overdue work hidden from automatic Today/reminders. Reopen requires a new non-past due date or explicit removal of the old date; dates/status update atomically and the Task leaves Overdue. Complete/archive also removes overdue membership.

components.label: Backlog
components.behavior: No deadline, start, occurrence or schedule date and not selected this week. Inbox is a parent/location concept and is independent of Backlog.

components.label: All
components.behavior: Default catalogue view when no valid view query is supplied. All fetched Tasks outside History, followed by independent search/status/tag filters and sorting. Open tasks hides Done rows in the main list; its separate Completed group uses the same view membership.

tests.symbol: test('backlog preserves inbox tasks but excludes selected and overdue tasks without inventing status'

components.label: Status and count badges
components.behavior: Stored Task statuses are NotStarted, InProgress, Blocked and Done. Open tasks excludes Done. Count badges apply the same view membership plus active search/status/tag filters; Repeating counts non-Ended series instead.

components.label: Completed section and History boundary
components.behavior: Under Open tasks, recently Done Tasks appear in a separate, independently paged section only when they match the selected Today/Next/Week/Backlog/All view. Search/tag/sort apply too. Overdue has no Done membership. History uses configurable elapsed completed-hours and local overdue-days thresholds; pruning remains a separate server job.

components.label: Inbox, Goal or Milestone parent
components.behavior: A Task has at most one Goal or Milestone parent; no parent is Inbox. Completed finite Goal ancestors reject new finite work. The server validates owned destinations even if the select was edited in the browser.

components.label: Task fields and estimates
components.behavior: The shared PHP partial renders schedule-related fields. Browser input is normalized by taskCaptureValues; server create/update validators enforce field bounds, unknown-key rejection and date ordering. Estimates represent planned minutes, not tracked time.

components.label: Due date, reminder and repeat picker
components.behavior: The schedule toolbar supplies presets and a draggable date picker. Reminders offer Later today, Tomorrow and Next week, moments tied to the task (when it starts, 15 minutes or 1 hour before its scheduled start, 9:00 on or the day before its due date; only future ones), and any date with any minute of the day in the device clock format. One-off capture POSTs a Task; repeat capture POSTs a TaskSeries. seriesPayload is the exact mapping boundary: do not assume every one-off field is copied into a series.

components.label: Name-first capture, Today/Week plan and result
components.behavior: Name comes first, then parent and Plan for. Today/Week views default Plan for to that view only for a clean draft; other views default Decide later. Optional description/criteria and advanced fields use native disclosure. The sticky Create/Cancel footer stays available while scrolling. A one-off Task is created before a separate daily/weekly selection; selection does not change its dates/status. If selection fails, creation is acknowledged once, the dialog closes, and an explicit partial-result message plus Open task link allows recovery without duplicate creation. Repeat disables Plan for; occurrences are selected individually. Successful series creation opens Repeating.
components.test_scope: Browser smoke on an isolated local account checked Today/Week capture and simulated a failed selection after a real create. No new backend transaction or cross-request atomicity is claimed.

components.label: Repeating list: Pause, Resume, End
components.behavior: Repeating uses name search plus an independent All/Active/Paused/Ended series-state select; Task status/sort/tag controls are hidden. The badge, list and pagination use the same filtered series, including Ended in All. Rows show series state, frequency, start/end and optional reminder time. Pause retains existing Tasks. Resume skips missed paused dates; End asks to archive future NotStarted occurrences, preserving started/Done work. Ended is terminal: API Pause/Resume returns 422 after ownership/version checks; repeated End with the current version is a no-op. Start a new series for future repeating work.

tests.symbol: test('Repeating search/state/count/paging use the same series including terminal rows'

components.label: Daily, weekly, monthly and yearly rules
components.behavior: Date calculation uses local calendar dates. Monthly/yearly dates clamp from the original anchor. Weekly carries weekdays. Local-time conversion resolves DST; the series/date unique key prevents duplicate occurrences. Preview calculates dates without querying or writing series/occurrence rows. Supported browser timezone aliases are canonicalized even when PHP accepts the alias directly; previously accepted fixed-offset forms keep their existing fallback behavior.

components.label: Initial and catch-up materialization
components.behavior: HTTP creation materializes immediately. The scheduler materializes hourly; Task listing and Dashboard reads also call materializeDue when the generated horizon is below 28 days. This read-path side effect is current code behavior. Generated work is excluded from finite Goal progress.

components.label: Overview and Edit dialog
components.behavior: Edits use a separate DraftBuffer. A save acknowledges only the submitted snapshot, retains newer typing and handles 409 through explicit saved/draft choices. Initial controls remain disabled until data loads.

tests.symbol: test('a late save acknowledgement preserves typing after the submitted snapshot'
tests.label: late save acknowledgement

tests.symbol: test('refresh cannot erase or silently rebase a dirty goal draft'
tests.label: refresh cannot erase

components.label: Complete and Reopen
components.behavior: Unchecked Checklist items require explicit acknowledgement. Completing a Task never checks items automatically. Reopening finite work beneath completed Goal ancestors asks to reopen those ancestors atomically. A locked Milestone does not block its Tasks. Reopening a Task with an overdue deadline requires choosing a non-past due date or clearing the old date in the shared workspace dialog, before any status/date write. Cancel preserves state.

components.label: Completion Checklist
components.behavior: Overview contains the completion Checklist beside the Task definition (stacked on mobile). Checklist records are separate owned/versioned rows. Check/uncheck writes Activity; order is a complete-ID-set mutation. This is distinct from inline checkable text in a working note.

components.label: Working note, Check box and Resources
components.behavior: Working notes and Resources remain only in the dedicated Notes tab; switching tabs preserves the current draft without moving/recreating the editor. The Task note uses explicit Save. Linking/creating the owned Note is handled by saveTaskNote; text persists through the Note API. Resource URLs are derived from plain note text. There is no promise of browser-crash recovery for this explicit-save editor.

tests.label: projection preserves

tests.symbol: test('toggling duplicate titles targets only its line and never changes literal note text'
tests.label: toggling duplicate titles

components.label: Tags, week selection and Related work
components.behavior: Tags and contributions classify or relate work without changing its primary location. Week selection controls This week; contributions do not affect progress.

components.label: Today and week planning actions
components.behavior: The header offers week selection and an icon-only Today toggle with native hover/accessibility labels. + adds Today; a check indicates membership. Explicit selections can be removed; automatic Today membership is disabled for removal here. Done disables Today selection. Actions reuse existing owned Dashboard selection APIs and change no Task dates/status.
components.test_scope: Real-browser smoke checked add/remove through the row and detail header on isolated local tasks.

components.label: Manage Areas
components.behavior: Accounts start with localized placeholder Areas. Rename/reorder uses owner/version checks; at most four active Areas and the last active Area cannot be archived. An Area containing active root Goals cannot be archived. Each Area has an importance of 1–5 (default 3), set with the stars beside its name in the Goal tree. Manage areas also exposes versioned icon/importance controls, compact Rename and Archive actions, and a Cancel-first Add area footer.

components.label: Goal tree, timeline and main Goal
components.behavior: Goal hierarchy has one primary Area or parent Goal and arbitrary depth. Tree/timeline presentation does not alter it: expand carets sit in a gutter so sibling Goals stay aligned and only sub-Goals are indented; deadlines read as localized dates. The Main goal card is the account's explicit focus Goal, the same choice as the Dashboard roadmap; its title is a picker that changes both, and with no choice it invites one instead of guessing by importance. Create/move validates ownership, active ancestors and cycles. Open a Goal name for its fishbone. New goal uses the shared floating creator with an Area preset; edit buttons on the Main goal card, tree and timeline open the same floating editor without changing roadmap navigation.

components.label: Icons, colours and importance stars
components.behavior: Areas, Goals, Milestones and Habits each take an optional icon from a fixed 39-symbol line set and one of eight accent colours; null keeps the automatic default (Areas and Milestones cycle the accents by position). The picker opens from the icon itself, saves immediately with the entity version, closes on Escape or an outside click and offers Use default icon. Tasks have no icon. Importance reads as 1–5 stars at every planning level, including Area (default 3); stars are editable where the entity is shown as a heading and read-only in lists. The server validates icon/icon_color against its catalogue (unknown values → 422) and the browser catalogue is tested to match it.

components.label: Fishbone, paging and Milestone focus
components.behavior: The owned roadmap projection separates finite and recurring Tasks, direct Tasks, child Goals and Habits. The browser renders six Milestone cards per page and switches layout for narrow screens. The Goal header carries its icon (click to change) and editable importance stars; each Milestone branch shows its icon, accent and stars, and the Milestone focus header edits both. Add milestone is the single primary header action and opens the shared creator with Goal/order presets. The fishbone head uses the chosen Goal icon.

tests.symbol: test('refresh cannot erase or silently rebase a dirty goal draft'
tests.label: refresh cannot erase

components.test_scope: Projection and shared draft behavior are covered here; fishbone SVG layout, paging and responsive interaction require a browser check.

components.label: Goal information: Edit, Strategy and Related work
components.behavior: Goal information keeps Strategy, Related work/notes and Tags in-page. Edit goal and all Goal/Milestone/Task creation use the shared floating editor, including parent-preserving sub-Goal creation; the old duplicate forms and capture suggestions are removed. Strategy retains its independent DraftBuffer, explicit Save, dirty-navigation guard and saved-version/draft conflict choices; it is plain text up to 20,000 code points and does not emit Activity or change progress.

components.label: Goal progress, completion and ancestor reopen
components.behavior: Progress is the mean of immediate active child Goal percentages, completed Milestones and Done direct one-off Tasks. Exclude Habits, contributions, occurrences and Tasks inside Milestones. Calculated 100% does not auto-complete the Goal.

components.label: Archive Goal and contents
components.behavior: Empty-container archive and include_contents=true are different operations. The latter explicitly archives descendant Goals, Milestones, Tasks and series and removes relevant prerequisite links in one transaction. It is not a hard delete or automatic default cascade.

components.label: Prerequisites and completion lock
components.behavior: Prerequisite edges form a separate acyclic graph and may cross owned Goals. All active prerequisites must be Completed to complete this Milestone. Reopening a prerequisite with a completed dependent is rejected; reopen dependents first.

components.label: Finite/recurring Tasks, weekly selection and Complete
components.behavior: Tasks under a locked Milestone are usable and completable. Completing a Milestone with unfinished Tasks requires acknowledge_open_tasks=true. Recurring occurrences do not enter finite completion denominators. Task rows share taskRowShell with Tasks: round completion tick, floating-editor name, status/due/repeat facts and read-only stars. Add task opens the shared creator with Milestone/order presets, replacing the duplicate capture dialog and suggestions.

components.label: Edit, contributions and archive
components.behavior: Milestone edits and contribution changes use aggregate versions. Archiving with include_contents is an explicit bulk action. Contributions never act as prerequisites or progress weights. Edit/Archive live in a keyboard-accessible disclosure menu; editing uses the shared floating editor. Week selection is an accessible pin toggle labelled Select for this week; Complete/Reopen is the primary panel action. Archive wording describes retained data and preserves include_contents confirmation.

components.label: Today progress and checklist
components.behavior: Today combines account-local daily selections, matching due/start/occurrence dates, overlapping work intervals and recent unfinished overdue work. Explicit daily selections remain visible even when a Task otherwise qualifies for History. Today and Weekly task rows use the existing versioned Complete/Reopen flow. On progress means InProgress; Scheduled means a planned start, occurrence or work interval today; a deadline alone is Due today. Completed rows retain their check state until the applicable membership/History boundary. Today owns one progress summary above its checklist: Done / full Today membership, including checked rows; an empty denominator is null and renders —. Current focus has been removed; Task completion/editing remains on the actual Task controls.

tests.symbol: test('Scheduled means planned start, occurrence or overlapping work interval, not deadline or reminder'

components.label: This week and weekly summary
components.behavior: The This week tab places its progress summary and Weekly tasks checklist in the main column, with Milestones/Habit targets and a Weekly activity chart in the side column. The chart shows the sum of daily contribution facts, seven readable weekday labels and per-day counts; zero dates have no green fill, and the account-local current date is highlighted. Column heights are relative to the largest count in that week, independently of checklist completion percentages. Today no longer contains any week content. Task rows support completion and Add for today without moving/removing weekly membership or changing Task dates/status. Two independent native selects sort by Importance (descending) or Scheduled time (earliest first, unscheduled last), and filter All/Not started/On progress/Blocked/Completed. Sorting/filtering does not rewrite stored order, membership or weekly percentage denominators; the count badge shows filtered/total while a status filter is active. The tab lists the whole selection (Today previews stay at four rows). The row action is a compact + icon with Add for today as its native hover tooltip and accessible name; already-present Tasks show a check mark. Filtering never changes the full selected denominator.

tests.symbol: test('weekly sort and status filter work independently without changing stored order'

components.label: Recent 30-day Activity and full year heatmap
components.behavior: A compact 30-day calendar replaces Current focus in the Today workspace. Its inclusive range ends on the account-local today, spans month/year boundaries and includes zero days. Counts are unreversed Task/Checklist/Habit/Milestone completion facts; Note edits do not count. Clicking a day shows its factual details; View activity switches to the existing full-year tab. The year grid/picker remains independent of the recent window. Existing activity colours/levels 0, 1, 2–3, 4–6, 7+ remain presentation, not a productivity score. The card balances the contribution total and active-day count with a Monday-first calendar, a Less/More legend and a separate details line. Recent and full-year calendars share light/dark colour variables; the selected recent date has an outline and aria-pressed state.

components.label: Habit streak and quick check-in
components.behavior: Today shows a Habits card beside Activity: the aggregate streak and its recent days, then each Habit with a checkbox that checks in or undoes today for that Habit's own local date (PUT/DELETE of the existing check-in route; Habit-local dates may differ from the account timezone). A day counts toward the streak only when every daily Habit is done or on a rest day. Rows show completed/target for the period, streak and rest-day state. Weekly Habits are checked in on individual days but their weekly target progress is read-only on the This week tab (Habit targets); weekly targets are never summed into a daily denominator. Creating, editing, resting and archiving remain on /habits.

components.label: Add task / Add for today
components.behavior: Choose an owned existing Task or create a named Inbox Task in the existing workspace-dialog style. POST accepts exactly an id or a name; new Task creation, daily selection and current Monday-week selection commit atomically. Existing-id desired-state replay is idempotent and never changes Task dates/status/version/Activity. The account timezone defines the implicit current date; caller-supplied dates are rejected. Removing a daily selection keeps the Task and weekly selection, and automatic date/schedule membership can still keep it in Today. There is no automatic next-day/week carry-forward.

components.label: Overdue reminder and encouragement
components.behavior: A compact line replaces the Needs attention panel. Only active unfinished Tasks with a past deadline that have not entered History count toward the reminder. Complete/archive removes a Task immediately; a new future deadline or clearing it removes overdue membership. When the reminder count is zero the line shows encouragement. The Overdue tasks link still exposes retained overdue work, including History-qualified Tasks, for an explicit Reopen. This is a Dashboard reminder policy, not a change to email/reminder delivery.

components.label: Roadmap below the header and account selection
components.behavior: The roadmap strip is directly below the page header, before the section tabs. A native select offers owned unarchived Goals, including child/completed Goals. Selection is stored per account; unset/cleared/archived choices show an invitation rather than automatically picking the highest-importance Goal. The preview shows up to six Milestones or the selected Goal link. The connector after each node fills green in proportion to that Milestone's own progress (Completed is 100%, otherwise finished Tasks over its Tasks); a node is solid when complete and outlined green when partly done. Progress is a factual Task ratio, not a prediction. Owner-locked PATCH validates exactly goal_id (owned UUID or null), returns 404 for foreign/archived IDs and does not modify Goal versions or planning facts. Stale Dashboard refreshes and obsolete preview requests cannot replace a newer choice. The same selection is the Goals page Main goal (GET /api/v1/dashboard/roadmap reads it).

tests.symbol: test('roadmap connector progress follows the Milestone, clamped to 0-100'

components.test_scope: HTTP coverage verifies persistence, ownership, CSRF, validation and archived-choice clearing. Browser evidence separately exercises reload, preview navigation and a deliberately delayed stale Dashboard refresh.

components.label: Team tasks assigned to you
components.behavior: The Daily tab lists open team Tasks assigned to the user across every active team Goal they joined (soonest due first, overdue highlighted), linking to that team Goal. The card is hidden when there are none; done Tasks, other members' Tasks and pending invitations never appear.

components.label: Month and week grid
components.behavior: Month (Monday-first weeks, no trailing empty week) and Week views with previous/next, Today and a Goal filter (All goals, one Goal, or Inbox). Each day lists Goal and Milestone deadlines first, then timed blocks by start time, then other Task dates; month cells show three items and +N more, which selects the day. Overdue due dates and deadlines are red; completed items are faded and struck through. Below 600px the month shows one dot per item and the selected day's list carries the detail; a week reads as a list of days. The view and date are kept in the address (view, date) and the view is remembered per browser.

components.label: Move by drag, keyboard or Move to…
components.behavior: An item moves by drag and drop onto a day or the selected-day panel, by Alt with an arrow key (one day left/right, one week up/down; focus follows the item), or with Move to… beside it in the day list, which opens the native date picker (the touch path). Each move sends one PATCH with the item's base_version and only the dates the move rule changes (see Move rule), then reloads; a stale version or invalid date range shows the server's message and the reloaded state. Moves are announced to screen readers.

components.label: Selected day, New task and Unscheduled
components.behavior: The side panel lists everything on the selected day with its kind, time and Goal or Milestone, and Add task. New task, Add task and double-clicking a day open the shared floating editor in create mode with the due date preset to that day and the filtered Goal as its parent. Clicking any item opens it in the floating editor instead of leaving the Calendar. Unscheduled lists open one-off Tasks with no date at all, by importance; dragging one onto a day, or Set due date, gives it that due date.

components.label: Gantt view by Goal, Milestone or Task
components.behavior: A third Calendar view beside Month and Week. Show by Goal (expand ▸ to Milestones, then Tasks), Milestone (expand to Tasks) or Task (work that ended before the timeline begins is left out); the Goal filter still applies. The name column stays put while the timeline scrolls sideways and grows as its end comes into view; zoom is Days, Weeks or Months, the arrows slide about a screen and Today returns. A Task spans its start date or slot to its due date or slot end; a Goal or Milestone spans its own start date to its deadline, taking a missing end from the work inside (drawn dashed, not draggable); a single date is a diamond. Bars look like Calendar items (icon, slot time, name), names stay readable at the visible left edge, overdue is red, done is faded and struck through, Goal and Milestone progress is a line along the bottom and prerequisite Milestones are joined by dashed links. Dragging a bar moves all of its own dates (a slot keeps its clock times), dragging an edge changes the start or the deadline without crossing the other; focused, Alt+←/→ moves by a day and Alt+Shift+←/→ changes the deadline. Each change is one versioned PATCH; Goal and Milestone start dates are validated not to fall after the deadline. Grouping and zoom are remembered per browser.

components.label: Habit cards and New/Edit dialog
components.behavior: The existing theme/cards and Edit fields are retained. Check-in sits before the name, which carries the Habit icon (click to change) and read-only importance stars; the calendar follows the text and moves below on narrower screens. Edit remains at the end; More options opens the existing secondary popover. Parent chips fit their text. Refresh is an icon with a native tooltip. Edit keeps Cancel then Save changes in a sticky footer on mobile. Daily target is one completion day; weekly target is 1–7 distinct days. Period/timezone freeze after the first check-in; archive/recreate to change them. Name, description, importance, Goal and Tags remain editable. New/edited timezone inputs normalize supported browser aliases to canonical identifiers. Equivalent input on a checked-in legacy Habit preserves its stored timezone and history; an actual timezone change remains rejected.

components.label: Check-in, undo and streak
components.behavior: The left-hand checkbox immediately checks in or undoes today, consistently with Dashboard; it no longer opens a menu. It exposes checkbox state and an action-specific accessible name. Calendar buttons retain dated check-in/undo. Controls disable during their request and restore focus after refresh. At most one check-in per Habit/local date. No future check-in; repeated PUT is idempotent. Undo reverses Activity. Streaks derive from check-ins and rest history, not a stored score.

components.label: More options and Rest Day window
components.behavior: More options exposes the next three Rest Day buttons and a separate Archive action. Selected rest dates can be canceled here or through the calendar. Escape closes the popover and returns focus to its trigger. A Rest Day can be planned only for tomorrow through local today+3. Today, past and later dates are rejected. A rest cannot hide an existing check-in or create completion Activity. The backend returns the available window.

components.label: Archive confirmation and retained history
components.behavior: Archive is secondary inside More options. Confirmation explains removal from active lists without deleting data; cancel performs no write. The existing owner/version-checked API timestamps the Habit and increments its version while retaining check-ins, rest days and Activity. Native PDO prepares require distinct archived_at/updated_at bindings even when their timestamp values are equal. A removed row returns keyboard focus to Refresh.

components.label: New review, type filter and pagination
components.behavior: Identity is owner/kind/period start, with timezone captured on creation. Period navigation does not redefine an existing Review when account timezone later changes. Demo seeding uses the same schema-one snapshot envelope and repository facts consumed by ReviewService/UI; ad hoc summary-only JSON is not a valid Review snapshot.

components.label: Reflections, Save and conflict choices
components.behavior: Reflection edits are explicit-save and versioned; newer typing stays dirty after an older save. Finalized Reviews must be reopened before editing. There is no Notes autosave state machine here.

components.label: Refresh facts, Finalize, Reopen and Delete
components.behavior: Refresh rebuilds Draft facts while preserving reflections. Finalize freezes the snapshot; Reopen does not refresh it automatically. Missing historical Goal snapshots remain unavailable. Delete is permanent and versioned.

components.label: All notes, search, sort, grid/list and paging
components.behavior: NotesPage owns loading, selection and read coordination. Browser layout preferences and server search/paging have separate state. Search/filter changes must not let stale responses replace the selected Note.

components.label: New note, title/content, color, pin and Save and close
components.behavior: NoteEditor and AutosaveMachine share the complete editable snapshot. Plain-text content supports inline checkable lines. Custom RGB, pin and labels remain owner-controlled; Save and close flushes the normal save path, then closes (as the close button and backdrop do). Permanent Delete sits apart, at the start of the action row. Card pin and live-collaboration color/pin/tag changes use the attribute endpoint, which never touches title/content. Cards show status icons for pinned, password-protected and shared Notes in grid and list views.

components.label: Note links to a Goal or Task
components.behavior: A Note can belong to one active Goal or Task of the same owner. The editor's Linked to picker sets or clears it outside the autosave snapshot (a new Note applies the choice after its first save); cards show the link as a chip, and Goal information and the Task Notes tab list linked Notes with a shortcut that opens a new Note already linked. Links to another account's work, or to both a Goal and a Task, are rejected; archiving or deleting the target hides or removes the link.

components.label: Delete and tombstones
components.behavior: Deleting an owned Note also unlinks its Task. A retried create with a tombstoned UUID returns 410 instead of resurrecting data. Pending file deletion is handled after the metadata transaction.

components.label: Dirty, saving, saved and retry state
components.behavior: Valid edits debounce at 500ms and dispatch within 2s of continuous typing. One logical request is frozen/in-flight at a time. Only exact acknowledged content is Saved. IME composition never sends partial text.

components.label: Recover draft, offline retry and session changes
components.behavior: One account-scoped sessionStorage record preserves acknowledged/draft/frozen request state. Validate schema, user, age and size before recovery. Retry exact requests after 1/2/4s, respect Retry-After, pause offline; validation/conflicts require intervention. Clear owned recovery records on logout/account change.

components.label: Saved-version/draft conflict decisions
components.behavior: Creates use stable client-generated UUIDs. Exact replay is a no-op; stale different updates return current owned content with 409. The editor keeps the local draft until the user chooses how to reconcile.

components.label: Share dialog: invite, permission and remove
components.behavior: Owner invites one or several registered accounts at once (comma-separated). Every address must belong to an account, otherwise nothing is written and the unknown addresses are named (422). New recipients get an in-app invitation and, when they allow it, an email. Owner can change view/edit or revoke access at any time; the list shows each recipient's email, permission and invited/accepted state. A deleted Note ends shares.

components.label: Shared with me, accept/decline, edit and leave
components.behavior: Shared with me lists accepted Notes with owner, permission (view only / can edit), share time and lock state; invitations can be accepted or declined. Edit recipients change title/content only: live over the realtime socket when available, otherwise by debounced autosave with base_version (a 409 retries on the newer version). View-only recipients see live updates read-only. Notes owned by a locked account are hidden from recipients (list and direct links return 404) until the account is unlocked; a moderator can also withdraw a reported Note from every recipient.

components.label: Report shared Note
components.behavior: A recipient reports a reason; the report stores a title/content snapshot. Admin review does not grant access to the live private Note.

components.label: Upload, select Note background and remove attachment
components.behavior: Server MIME/signature and size validation is authoritative; attachment limit is 20MiB. Metadata transactions compensate failed writes; deferred deletion avoids mixing file I/O with SQL commits.

components.label: Preview, download, HEAD and Range
components.behavior: Only allowed media types preview. Safe filenames and a single byte Range are supported; 206/416 and HEAD preserve streaming semantics. Path traversal, foreign IDs and symlinks are rejected.

components.label: Tag picker, hierarchy and Notes labels
components.behavior: Names are normalized and owner-unique. Tag moves reject cycles; complete tag_ids snapshots belong to their aggregate mutation. `/api/v1/labels` remains a compatibility API over the same rows.

pages.title: /teamwork — Team Goals, members, Tasks and chat

components.label: Team Goal cards, search and carousel
components.behavior: The browser filters names/descriptions and pages up to four cards (two below 900px, one below 560px). Selecting a card loads one team Goal; responsive layout does not change access rights.

tests.symbol: test('team goal search matches every word in the name or description'
tests.label: team goal search

tests.symbol: test('the carousel shows at most four goals and pages through them four at a time'
tests.label: carousel shows

components.label: Invite, accept/decline, role, remove and completion
components.behavior: Members have admin/member/viewer roles. Team admins manage membership; the creator cannot be removed/demoted by the normal flow. Member biography and factual done/assigned counts are shown. A locked account stays a member, shown as Locked, keeps the work already assigned to it and cannot be chosen for new work.

components.label: Assigned Task capture, status, due/reminder and repeat
components.behavior: Team members/admins may create Tasks; assignment is team-scoped. An assignee, including a viewer, may change only their own status through the allowed status-only path. Personal TaskSeries logic does not run here.

tests.symbol: test('team task payload reuses the Tasks capture fields and adds the assignee'
tests.label: team task payload

components.label: Team chat and polling
components.behavior: Messages are plain text, 1–2000 characters. The open chat polls every 5 seconds; this is not WebSocket collaboration. Chat/reminder notifications are user-scoped.

components.label: Display name and biography
components.behavior: Profile PATCH accepts display_name and optional biography (up to 2,000 code points); omission preserves biography. Save feedback belongs to this form.

components.label: Replace and remove avatar
components.behavior: Avatar upload validates and re-encodes the image, stores it privately and serves the current account through /files/avatar. Queue removal after metadata changes.

components.label: Verification status, resend and change email
components.behavior: Changing email requires current_password, emails a confirmation link to the new address and notifies the old address after confirmation. Never expose tokens in docs or public screenshots.

components.label: Theme, light/dark, scenery and illustration toggles
components.behavior: Appearance is account-persisted. applyAppearance consumes acknowledged preferences; decoration is not authoritative product data. Keep CSS selectors and preference serialization in sync.

components.label: Private backgrounds, Add tile, RGB and reset
components.behavior: Up to 12 owned backgrounds are retained. Upload validates JPEG/PNG/WebP, <=2MiB and <=4096x4096, re-encodes privately and serves only the owner. RGB is #RRGGBB; a submitted external URL/path is not accepted.

components.label: Personal quote, preset restore and locale
components.behavior: Quote text requires explicit Save; theme/toggles save independently. Preserve newer quote drafts while a save is pending. Locale changes UI literals, not stored user content.

tests.symbol: test('every literal interface string has a Vietnamese translation'
tests.label: every literal interface string

components.label: Change password and visibility toggle
components.behavior: Require current password and exact confirmation, at least 10 code points, at most 72 bytes, no NUL. A successful change bumps auth_version and deletes sessions atomically; redirect to sign in.

components.label: Set up email codes or TOTP, confirm and disable
components.behavior: TOTP secret is encrypted and setup becomes active only after a valid code. Email codes are hashed, single-use and attempt/expiry limited. Disabling requires the current password. Pending login is separate from an authenticated session.

components.label: Delete my account
components.behavior: Settings › Security ends with Delete account: the current password, a tick that the data cannot be recovered and a final confirmation delete the account and everything it owns for good, then the browser returns to sign-in. Administrator accounts see an explanation instead (their role is removed with the server console first). Wrong passwords are refused; the route uses the password-change rate limit.

components.label: Notifications, invitation emails and Task reminders
components.behavior: Preferences control new in-app rows and opted-in email delivery. Admin report notifications are always created. Personal Task reminder emails require the scheduler and configured transport; team Task reminders are in-app only.

components.label: Completed-hours, overdue-days and retention settings
components.behavior: Rules are available in a collapsed History rules panel below retrieval results. Defaults are 24 elapsed completed-hours and 3 local overdue-days. Retention is optional; the admin history cap still applies. Changing thresholds changes membership without rewriting Task completion facts.

tests.symbol: test('history uses elapsed completion time and local calendar overdue dates'
tests.label: history uses elapsed

components.label: Search, detail navigation and Reopen
components.behavior: Search and results precede rules; Back to Tasks returns to the catalogue. The client derives History membership, searches names/descriptions, and pages 12 rows in descending completion time (Done) or due date (unfinished), with a stable ID tie-break. Search resets the page; reopen/filter changes clamp it. The client derives History membership and filters names/descriptions. Every retained historical Task offers Reopen. If its old deadline is overdue, the server requires a new non-past date or explicit null to clear it; no write occurs while the decision is pending or canceled. Replanning unfinished work does not invent a completion reversal. Completed Task reversal and ancestor acknowledgements remain authoritative.

tests.symbol: test('history uses elapsed completion time and local calendar overdue dates'
tests.label: history uses elapsed

tests.symbol: test('reopening an overdue Task sends the chosen date with existing acknowledgement and version'
test('History sorts completion/due facts newest first, searches descriptions and clamps pages after reopen'

components.label: Report form with image evidence
components.behavior: The reporter names a person by email, describes the problem (10–2000 characters) and may attach up to 3 JPEG/PNG/WebP images (5 MB each, re-encoded to JPEG without metadata). The answer is identical whether or not the email has an account. Self-reports and a second open report about the same email are rejected.

components.label: The reporter's own reports and replies
components.behavior: Lists the reporter's reports with status and the administrator reply; never shows whether the email matched an account.

components.label: Archived items, type filter and search
components.behavior: Lists the owner's archived Areas, Goals, Milestones, Tasks and Habits newest first (up to 500 per type) with kind, status, archive time and where each lived. Contents archived together with a Goal or Milestone are folded into it as a count. A type filter (Everything, Areas, Goals, Milestones, Tasks, Habits) and a name search page through 12 items at a time; items inside an archived parent say which parent to restore first and their Restore button is disabled.

tests.symbol: test('archive filters by type and name

components.label: Restore with its group, parents first
components.behavior: Restore sends the item's version. The server locks the owner, refuses an item that is not archived, changed (409), belongs to someone else (404) or lives inside an archived parent (422 naming it), and an Area while four are active. A Goal or Milestone comes back with the sub-Goals, Milestones and Tasks archived with it; the page reports how many items returned and reloads. Archiving with contents uses one timestamp for the whole group so the group can be restored exactly.

components.label: Delete for good and Empty archive
components.behavior: Each archived item has Delete for good, and Empty archive deletes everything archived; both ask first and cannot be undone. An item goes with everything beneath it, all of which is archived (an active row reached on the way stops and rolls back the whole deletion). Habits that supported a deleted Goal and a Dashboard roadmap pointing at it only lose that link; Activity facts stay. Deletion follows the schema's foreign keys in one transaction with checks on, queues private files and removes them after the commit. Owner-only (404), version-checked (409), the empty call needs confirm=true.

components.label: /login — Sign in
components.behavior: Generic failures do not reveal whether an email exists. Password visibility is a shared client helper. Rate limits apply by email/IP and IP; locked accounts cannot authenticate.

components.label: /register — Create account
components.behavior: Registration creates owned preferences/default Areas transactionally, stores guest language, sends a verification link and establishes the normal session. Public registration does not grant system-admin role. An administrator decides who may register: Anyone with the link (default), Only invited emails, or Nobody. By invitation, the email must be on the admin's invitation list, and each invitation creates one account; closed hides the form and the Login page's sign-up link. The server enforces the mode inside the registration transaction.

components.label: Logout and account/session changes
components.behavior: Logout is POST with CSRF. Clear this account/tab recovery state and notify other tabs; do not erase unrelated browser storage.

components.label: Forgot password and reset form
components.behavior: Known/unknown valid emails receive the same response. The email carries a link and a 6-digit code; either leads to the new-password form. Tokens and codes are stored hashed, expire after 30 minutes and are single-use; a code dies after five wrong guesses. Reset changes password, auth_version and sessions atomically; it does not automatically log in.

components.label: Email verification and address-change confirmation
components.behavior: Verification links expire after 24h; address-change links after 1h. The service validates ownership/purpose/expiry before applying changes. Invalid/expired links render 422. Never copy live tokens into examples.

components.label: Verify TOTP/email code or request fallback
components.behavior: TOTP permits the configured time-step window. Email fallback uses a hashed, expiring, limited-attempt code. The challenge cannot be bypassed by loading a protected page directly.

pages.title: Shared — Layout, CSS, navigation and Help

components.label: Sidebar, topbar, mobile navigation and page bootstrap
components.behavior: AccountController renders page shell/bootstrap; page modules load their own data. Keep root-relative navigation, owned session state and existing data hooks stable.

components.label: Typography, themes and component CSS
components.behavior: CSS entry imports tokens/base/layout/components/feature styles. Change shared tokens for cross-app values; edit feature sheets for scoped presentation. Vite serves source in local mode and hashed /build assets for production.
components.test_scope: Manifest/CSP checks do not certify visual rendering or typography; inspect browser loading and appearance separately.

components.label: Dialogs, sections, Escape, backdrop and leave guards
components.behavior: workspace-ui and dialog-backdrop manage common interactions. Dirty/save/conflict flows are owned by each editor; preserve focus and drafts when moving components.

tests.label: creation drafts

tests.symbol: test('creation serializes a pending write and restores the original controls after failure'
tests.label: creation serializes

tests.symbol: test('only clicks beyond the dialog box count as backdrop clicks'
tests.label: only clicks beyond

components.label: Help tour and first-visit dismissal
components.behavior: The ? button opens a short tour of twelve steps, each with a real screenshot in the account language (walkthrough-content shot names, /guide/<language>/<shot>.webp) and alternative text; Open the full guide leads to /help. Other dialogs and draft recovery take priority. Skip/Close/Escape/Finish persist account-wide dismissal once.

tests.symbol: test('every tour step is written in both languages

components.label: Floating editor for Tasks, Goals and Milestones
components.behavior: One side sheet (full screen below 600px) edits or creates a Task, Goal or Milestone on the current page. Calendar items, Tasks rows and their Edit item, Dashboard task rows and the roadmap's Milestone task list open it on a plain click; a modified click (Ctrl, Cmd, Shift, middle button) keeps the full page, and Open full page leads there for working notes, Related work and history. Task: name, Add to (Inbox, Goal or open Milestone), status, importance stars, start/due dates, scheduled start/end, reminder, estimate, description, criteria and the completion checklist (tick or add). Goal and Milestone: icon, name, importance, deadline, description and criteria; a new Goal picks its Area and a new Milestone its Goal, while moving them stays on the roadmap. Save sends only the changed fields with base_version; Complete/Reopen use the ordinary transitions and their confirmations. A version conflict keeps the draft and offers Use saved version or Keep my draft, which lays only the fields edited here over the latest version. Closing with unsaved changes asks first; Escape inside the icon picker closes only the picker. Every save dispatches planner:changed, which refreshes the Calendar, Tasks, Goals, Dashboard and roadmap in place. Goals and roadmap creation also use this sheet; sub-Goals retain parent_goal_id rather than selecting an Area, and roadmap Milestone/Task creations preserve their append-position presets.

components.test_scope: Form value and change mapping are unit-tested; opening, saving, conflicts, checklist and transitions were exercised in a browser.

components.label: User guide page per language
components.behavior: A signed-in article with a sticky table of contents: overview and purpose, getting started, the screen, how the parts fit together (a table of what each item is, where it lives and its rules, plus what Planner promises), one section per use case with numbered steps and screenshots, administration and frequently asked questions. The account language picks guide-vi or guide-en; screenshots come from /guide/<language>/ and open full size. Below 900px the contents stack above the article and wide tables scroll inside their section.

components.label: Demo accounts and screenshot pipeline
components.behavior: seed-demo.php builds the Vietnamese and English demo accounts through the ordinary services (with helper accounts for sharing and Teamwork) and refuses to run twice; capture.mjs signs in with Playwright and captures each listed shot per language; publish.php converts them to WebP under backend/public/guide and removes stale ones. Tests fail when the guide or the tour references a screenshot that was not published.

tests.symbol: test('every tour step is written in both languages

components.label: Unread count, list, mark read and invitations
components.behavior: The bell polls every 60s while visible, displays the latest 50 and routes invitation actions through sharing/team APIs. Notifications are user-owned; admin report notifications bypass ordinary opt-out. New notifications carry params (who, which note or team, permission, role, report outcome) and the bell words them in the reader's language; older ones without params show their stored text.

tests.symbol: test('notifications are worded in the reader language from their params'

components.label: Due personal/assigned team reminders and dismissal
components.behavior: Due reminders are derived from Tasks and merged into the bell. Dismissal uses reminder_read_at independently from email reminder_sent_at. Changing time or assignee makes a new reminder visible. Team reminders are in-app only.

pages.title: Shared — Floating AI assistant and proposal APIs

components.label: Tool-calling chat, owned reads and conversation history
components.behavior: The chat sends the recent conversation as real turns. AIChatService runs up to six model rounds over owner-scoped read tools (including get_roadmap) and queues supported writes into a proposal instead of mutating domain data. Create tools return refs so a Goal, its ordered Milestones and their Tasks are queued together; sub-Goals standing in for requested Milestones and delete-and-recreate restructures are refused. Disabled mode reports unavailable; provider calls do not bypass normal ownership. Preview and explicit Apply/Cancel live in the floating chat.

components.label: Chat proposal preview, Apply and Cancel
components.behavior: The chat card previews queued supported create/update/transition/archive operations for Goals/Milestones/Tasks/Habits, Task moves, Milestone order and create/update/delete for Notes. Apply sends the exact version/hash; AIActionService validates ownership, context versions and expiry before ordinary services run atomically, appending new Milestones and Tasks in proposal order. Cancel calls Reject; replay retains stored outcomes. Dates and local time slots on the card read like the rest of Planner (for example “Nov 7, 7:00 PM”); the chat waits up to 90 seconds for a multi-round answer. No queued write executes just because the model proposed it. Existing standalone structured creation APIs remain available.

tests.symbol: test('proposal cards show dates and local time slots like the rest of Planner'

components.label: Calendar scheduling from the chat
components.behavior: The assistant can act on the Calendar. create_tasks and update_task accept start_date and a scheduled block (scheduled_start/scheduled_end) given as local wall-clock times in the account timezone; clear_schedule removes the block. reschedule moves up to 30 Tasks, Milestones or Goals by shift_days or to_date with the Calendar move rule: every date of an item moves by the same number of days and a block keeps its local clock times across daylight saving; with to_date the item's first Calendar date lands on that day and an undated item gets it as its due date. Done or completed items, times in the past, landing days before today and inverted ranges are refused before anything is queued. Changes appear on the confirmation card as Reschedule with local times and run only on Apply, through the ordinary versioned updates.

components.label: Open/resolved reports and resolution
components.behavior: List report snapshots, reason, reporter/owner (with lock state) and date. An open report has a resolution form: choose actions — Stop sharing this note with everyone (removes every share, including pending invitations), Warn the owner (an always-delivered notification that never names the reporter) and Lock the owner’s account — add an optional reply, then Resolve or Dismiss. Resolve requires at least one action unless the owner is already locked; Dismiss takes none. The reporter is told “reviewed and action was taken” or “reviewed. No action was needed” accordingly. The actions taken are stored with the report and shown as chips once handled, and each one is recorded in Administrator activity.

components.label: User reports with image evidence
components.behavior: List reports filed from Settings: reported email, matched account (or none), reporter, reason and evidence thumbnails served only to admins. Resolve with Warn this account and/or Lock this account (or because the account is already locked), or Dismiss with no action; an optional reply goes to the reporter, whose notification says whether action was taken. A report whose email matches no account can only be dismissed. Actions are stored with the report and recorded in Administrator activity.

components.label: Search users, lock/unlock
components.behavior: Locking bumps auth_version and deletes sessions; locked users cannot sign in or keep existing sessions. It also hides the Notes they shared from every recipient and marks them Locked in Teams, where they keep existing work but cannot be assigned new tasks; unlocking restores both. The list shows who locked an account and why. Self-lock is rejected, and administrators cannot be locked here: the role is granted and removed only with the server console (users:role), so one administrator cannot shut another out. Team roles do not grant these endpoints.

components.label: System Task history limit
components.behavior: The admin can set the history cap (100–10000, default 1000). The history maintenance job applies it in addition to per-user retention. It archives Tasks, not hard-deletes them.

components.label: Registration mode and invitations
components.behavior: Registration sets who can create an account: Anyone with the link, Only invited emails or Nobody (closed). Invited emails are listed with Waiting for sign-up or Account created and who used them; an unused invitation can be removed, and an email that already has an account cannot be invited. The operator can set the same mode with php bin/console registration:mode [open|invite|closed] before exposing a new host. Every change is recorded in Administrator activity.

components.label: Administrator activity
components.behavior: An append-only record of administration, newest first (100 entries): locks and unlocks, warnings, withdrawn shares, report resolutions and dismissals, setting changes, invitations, and role or registration changes made with the server console (shown as Server console). Each entry has the time, the actor and a short summary; it never stores report evidence or Note content.

components.label: Delete an account
components.behavior: Beside Lock, Delete account removes an ordinary account for good after the administrator types its email (case and spaces ignored). Administrators, including oneself, cannot be deleted here. Everything the account owns goes, with its files; so do its shares with others and team goals it created (for their members too). Reports about it and administrator history stay with the link cleared. Recorded in Administrator activity as Deleted an account.

components.label: Password: turn on, change, remove and unlock
components.behavior: Owner turns on a per-Note password by typing it twice (4+ characters, bcrypt). Changing needs the current password plus the new one twice; removing needs the current password. Opening, editing, deleting, pinning, sharing, attachments, AI summary and realtime tickets of a locked Note answer 423 until this session enters its password; the unlock is remembered for 15 idle minutes and dropped when the editor closes or the password changes. Cards, search, linked lists, AI questions and the offline copy never contain locked text. Wrong guesses are limited per account and Note.

components.label: Live co-editing of shared Notes
components.behavior: Opening a shared Note (owner or accepted recipient) requests a 60-second HMAC ticket and connects to bin/realtime.php over WebSocket. Title and content are separate OT documents: the server sequences operations, transforms concurrent ones, acknowledges and broadcasts them, shows who is present and a named caret where each collaborator types in the content and saves the merged text through NoteService after typing pauses (at most every 3 s and when the last person leaves). Reconnects rebase unsent edits; access is re-checked every few seconds. If the server cannot be reached, editing continues with normal autosave.

tests.symbol: test('several clients editing concurrently converge with the server'
tests.label: client convergence

components.label: AI summary of one Note
components.behavior: The editor (and the shared-note dialog) shows the stored summary and generates or regenerates it with the configured LLM in the Note's own language. The summary is shared by everyone who can read the Note and is marked out of date when the title or content changed since (pin/color do not count). Locked Notes need their password first.

components.label: Ask AI about your Notes
components.behavior: A question searches the user's unlocked Notes and accepted shared Notes by meaning (embeddings, cached per text) and keywords (accent-insensitive BM25), sends the best eight to the LLM and shows a synthesized answer with clickable source Notes. Only Notes actually given to the model can be cited; locked Notes are never read. Without embeddings it falls back to keywords.

components.label: Offline Notes, queued changes and sync
components.behavior: A service worker caches built assets and recent pages; the Notes page keeps an IndexedDB copy per account filled from the cursor-based sync feed. Offline, the list (search, tags, order) and editor work from that copy; creates, edits and deletes are queued, one entry per Note, and replayed on reconnect. A version conflict saves the offline text as an “(offline copy)”. Locked text and files are not stored offline. Logout clears caches and the local copy.

tests.symbol: test('offline edits of one note become a single request'
tests.label: outbox
